commonErrors.why: You multiply the coefficient by the mass directly. Friction depends on the normal force in newtons, not on the mass in kilograms. The mass must be multiplied by g first.
You wrote the normal force and did not multiply it by the coefficient.
You divided by the coefficient instead of multiplying by it. The coefficient is smaller than one, so friction is smaller than the normal force, not larger.
You used the entire mg. This is true on a horizontal surface alone; On a slope, the surface carries only the vehicle perpendicular to it, which is smaller than the weight.
You used sine instead of cosine and calculated the component parallel to the surface. To verify: at θ = 0, N must equal the full weight, and the sine gives zero.
You neglected g and calculated m cos θ, and the unit of your result is not newtons.

questions.solution: mg sin θ = 5.0 × 9.8 × 0.5 = 24.5 N, which pushes the body down the slope.

commonErrors.why: You used cosine and calculated the component perpendicular to the surface. The parallel component is accompanied by the sine function.
You wrote the entire weight without factoring. The weight is vertical, and the surface is inclined, so it must be factored on both axes.
You wrote the gravitational acceleration instead of the force component.

questions.solution: tan θ_c = μ_s = 1.0, and the angle with a tangent of one is 45°. Notice that the mass does not enter the calculation at all.

commonErrors.why: You wrote the value of the parameter. The parameter is the tangent of the angle, not the angle itself.
Upright slope means free fall; There is no surface in contact with the body at all, so there is no friction.
At zero slope, the surface is horizontal and no vehicle is pushing the body, so there is no sliding.

questions.solution: N = 20 × 9.8 = 196 N, and maximum static friction 0.50 × 196 = 98 N. Any force exceeding 98 N starts motion.
